weaknesses.title: Orphan path.lock after process crash wedges all agents — no dead-owner reclaim
weaknesses.detail: LOCKFILE creates .lock then process exit without UNLOCK leaves file. Next LOCKFILE waits/timeouts forever until manual RM. No PID liveness check or break-stale.
weaknesses.repro: LOCKFILE p; kill -9; LOCKFILE p 100 → timeout

weaknesses.title: lease_lock TOUCH vs LOCKFILE dual exclusion models
weaknesses.detail: TOUCH-based lease_lock is TOCTOU; LOCKFILE is exclusive. Agents mixing both on same path get false safety.

weaknesses.title: held is EXIST(.lock) not flock ownership probe
weaknesses.detail: Orphan .lock reports held=yes even though no live owner. Agents skip work incorrectly or spin waitfree forever.

weaknesses.title: WRITEATOMIC under lock still omits trailing NL
No path join for .lock suffix — agents use SUBSTENV ${active}.lock glue
weaknesses.detail: SYS JOIN treats .lock as path segment. Language lacks STRCAT/suffix helper for lock path derivation.

weaknesses.title: WAITGONE busy-poll; dual of WAITFILE naming easy to invert
weaknesses.detail: waitfree vs wait-present confusion under stress.

weaknesses.title: UNLOCK soft free is OK=1 N=0 — same soft shape as success
weaknesses.detail: Agents must check UNLOCKFILE_N; easy to treat free unlock as success.

workarounds: Always UNLOCK in finally path; RM orphan .lock on deploy recovery
Prefer LOCKFILE over TOUCH lease for true exclusion
Gate on LOCKFILE_HIT and UNLOCKFILE_N not only OK
Derive lock path via SUBSTENV ${path}.lock not JOIN
language_gaps: LOCKFILE break or force-unlock admin op
held = live owner not mere EXIST
Document flock vs create-exclusive semantics in help
